title: Decouple lint/test bootstrap and introduce dep-anchor autopilot
author: Noah Alvarez
description: Context: Our presubmit pipeline currently couples lint/toolchain bootstrapping with heavy integration test setup. That causes long cold-start latency and unnecessary installs for changes that only touch docs, API surface hints, or front-end TypeScript. Motivation: reduce CI cost and developer feedback time by one order of magnitude for common fastpaths (styling/TS lint, formatting, small docs edits) while preserving strong end-to-end test coverage for substantive changes. What this PR does: 1) Split the CI bootstrap into two explicit lanes: a lightweight lint bootstrap and a full-runtime bootstrap. The lightweight lane installs only the minimal toolchain and language servers required by the lint runner; the full lane remains unchanged for integration and e2e tests. 2) Introduce a new small service/tooling "dep-anchor" (tools/dep-anchor) that maintains a canonical anchored dependency set for Node/Python/Rust devdeps. The dep-anchor provides: - an anchored manifest (anchored-devdeps.json) that CI can consume to avoid noisy, repeated dependency churn - a weekly rotation job that opens proposed PRs to update minor/patch versions with a curated changelog and test matrix - a small CLI that validates a workspace against the anchor manifest (used as a presubmit guard) 3) Add a lint-runner adaptor (ci/lint-adaptor) to express plugin requirements per package; this prevents installing the entire monorepo toolchain for single-package linting. 4) Hooked dep-anchor integrity as a soft pre-release gate in the release workflow: the release job will include a diff of anchored devdeps and annotate release notes. Migration plan: - Phase 1 (this PR): opt-in: new lightweight lint workflow runs in parallel but does not replace existing presubmit lanes. Dep-anchor runs in read-only mode and creates PRs under tools/dep-anchor/cron/ when relevant. - Phase 2 (2 weeks after rollout): make lightweight lint the default fastpath for changed-files-only lint triggers, fall back to full bootstrap on diagnostic failures. - Rollback: revert the CI workflow file (.github/workflows/ci-split-lint.yml) and disable the scheduled dep-anchor cron job; dep-anchor changes are PR-driven and easy to revert. Testing performed: - Local smoke runs of lightweight bootstrap across 6 representative packages (python/core, ts/sdk, go/sdk, docs, infra) - End-to-end CI run in a feature branch with both lanes enabled (initial failures fixed in follow-up commit) - Unit tests for dep-anchor CLI and the anchor validation hook - Manual verification of weekly-PR flow against a sandbox repo Observability & metrics: added lightweight metrics emitted by the lint adaptor (latency_ms, bootstrap_pkg_count) and dep-anchor (anchor_hash, pr_count_last_7d) so we can measure cost and PR noise. Security & compliance notes: dep-anchor writes no secrets; it pins transitive devdeps but does not modify production dependency graphs. The PR includes docs for maintainers and a short on-call playbook for resolving an accidental bulk update. Shipping notes: this is intended to reduce CI minutes and improve developer iteration times. See release_notes for the concise user-facing summary.
commit_summary: a. ci: add .github/workflows/ci-split-lint.yml (lightweight lint lane, full lane preserved); b. tools/dep-anchor: initial CLI, anchor manifest schema, weekly cron job skeleton; c. ci: introduce ci/lint-adaptor config and package-level plugin hints; d. docs: CONTRIBUTING.md update and dep-anchor README; e. tests: unit tests for dep-anchor validation and adaptor bootstrap; f. fix: update a handful of packages to satisfy stricter lint runner requirements; g. small telemetry hooks for metrics export
review_comments: Morgan Patel (reviewer): Strong +1 on the direction. Two asks: 1) can we make the lightweight lane the default for 'docs-only' changes in a follow-up; 2) dep-anchor needs a simple explainable algorithm in the README for how it chooses candidate updates?

Noah Alvarez (author): Answered: agree on (1) and it's part of Phase 2; added an algorithmic sketch to tools/dep-anchor/README.md (heuristic: prefer non-breaking semver bumps, skip major changes without explicit maintainers tag).
Evelyn Ross (reviewer): CI failure on first run - lint adaptor threw plugin resolution error for packages/ts/sdk. Request: add a CI probe that verifies adaptor resolution before running lint stage.
Noah Alvarez (author): Added a preflight resolution probe step and fixed package hint for packages/ts/sdk. Rerun CI - green. See commit 'ci: add adaptor preflight probe'.

Priya Singh (reviewer): Small nit: add an example of how an external contributor can run dep-anchor locally and preview the PR changes. Also please add a unit test for anchor manifest schema validation.
Noah Alvarez (author): Added 'dep-anchor preview --dry-run' docs and a unit test for schema. Ready for merge.
Evelyn Ross (approver): Approved after CI green and documentation updates. Noted we should watch the weekly PR cadence for noise.
Morgan Patel (maintainer): Merged with rebase. Leaving a follow-up ticket to add metrics dashboard (ENG-2210).
release_notes: Reduced CI cold boot time for lint-only changes by introducing a lightweight lint bootstrap. Added 'dep-anchor' tooling to stabilize dev dependency churn and auto-propose safe rotations. Opt-in rollout with phase plan; metrics added to observe impact.
